newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to ease ban on U.S. lawyers practising.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to ease ban on U.S. lawyers practising.

text.p: Taiwan agreed Monday to ease its ban on foreign lawyers practicing on the island as part of its efforts to open its services market and join the World Trade Organisation, a state-funded news agency reported.
The initial agreement was reached on the last day of a four-day meeting with the United States on Taiwan's bid to join the WTO.

Foreign lawyers will be allowed to practice in Taiwan here as long as they have been in full service for three years in their home countries, the Central News Agency quoted the vice-chairman of the Council for Economic Planning and Development, Chi Schive, as saying.
But these people need to serve as "assistant lawyers" for two years before they can be officially allowed to practise in Taiwan, the agency quoted Schive as saying.
The two sides still had differences over Taiwan's import of more beef, chicken and offal, the agency said.
In its talks on January 30, Taiwan agreed to an American demand that it lift its ban on print alcohol advertisements and ease restrictions on television commercials for alcohol.
The two sides will hold further talks on services, finance and imports in early March, the agency said.
Taiwan, keen to join the WTO in 1997, has completed necessary bilateral talks with 12 of the 26 WTO members that have sought such a dialogue with Taipei.
Taiwan applied in 1990 to join the organisation's predecessor, the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade.
